svg.aria-label: Curves of the exponent M of k and N divided by k for N from 2 to 6, plotted against k. At k = 1 every curve is zero; at k = minus 1 every curve from N = 3 on is zero and N = 2 is minus 1.
svg.text: Strength of the singularity at ρ/N, as k turns
N = 2 gives −1: a plain pole (the ζ(2s) in ζ(s)/ζ(2s))
The exponent at ρ/N (one ζ zero there) is M(k,N)/k. A whole number means a pole or a zero;
any other value means a branch point. Only at k = ±1 do all but finitely many vanish.
